newsitem.title: UK: Air cargo 'known shipper' concept too loose-TIACA.
newsitem.headline: Air cargo 'known shipper' concept too loose-TIACA.

text.p: The known shipper definition used in the air cargo industry is too loose and needs tightening to increase safety although this may be costly, the chairman of the International Air Cargo Association (TIACA) security committee said.

"The loss of one life as a result of a breach in security is unacceptable. Making our industry more secure will be a burden on all segments of the industry. There is no alternative," C Brown Wilder said in a statement issued from the Miami-based TIACA.

The focus on security of the air cargo industry is "absolutely appropriate" and may be costly to all segments of the industry, Wilder who is president and CEO of Air Cargo Inc (ACI) reported to the Miami based TIACA.
Wilder and ACI vice-president Kent Jones gave TIACA an update on the work of the U.S. Cargo Baseline Working Group made up of lawyers and industry experts.
This group was set by and reports to the Gore Commission formed after last year's ValuJet and TWA airline crashes. TIACA said improper cargo caused the ValuJet crash.
Wilder said the group believed a tightening of the known shipper definition wold eliminate the need for the known shipper to complete a security endorsement.
It also wants either the U.S. Federal Aviation Authority (FAA) or an independent third party to oversee and enforce any improvements in cargo security on passenger flights.
The FAA has hired 130 new inspectors to improve oversight and enforcement of rules now mainly covering dangerous goods.
TIACA said the air cargo industry is awaiting new FAA recommendations including ones on the known shipper concept, training, small packages, and ground vehicle security.
